Monte Carlo methods approximate quantities by repeated random sampling. They connect [[Probability]] to practical [[Statistics]].

## Sampling

For samples $X_1, \ldots, X_n$, estimate an expectation with

$$
\widehat{\mu}_n = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i.
$$

::: {#cell-monte-carlo-estimate .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
draws = [0.41, 0.48, 0.52, 0.55]
estimate = sum(draws) / len(draws)
estimate
```

::: {#monte-carlo-estimate .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
0.49
```
:::
:::


## Convergence

The approximation generally improves as the number of samples grows. See [[Bayesian Inference]] for a common application.

::: {#cell-convergence-data .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
sample_sizes = [10, 100, 1000]
errors = [0.18, 0.06, 0.02]
dict(zip(sample_sizes, errors))
```

::: {#convergence-data .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
{10: 0.18, 100: 0.06, 1000: 0.02}
```
:::
:::
